$comment: Every command whose caller waits for an answer, and whether the producer
could have answered it without waiting.
WHY THIS EXISTS. Two decisions rest on this number and neither can be made
from an impression of it.
The first is Apple E1. Content on the Performance+ lane runs in an agent
inside WebKit's WebContent process, and the choice between a Dedicated
Worker and the Window agent is not a performance trade: the Window main
agent's [[CanBlock]] is false, so Atomics.wait throws there and a
synchronous reply is not slower, it is impossible. So the size of this
table is the size of what the Window lane would have to drop. E1 was
written naming four examples; the derived count is what it should have
named.
The second is Android, today. A command that waits stalls the JavaScript
thread for a round trip, and two of these -- ClientWaitSync and
GetQueryParameter -- are designed to be polled every frame. Adding one more
is a per-frame cost that nothing else in the build will report.
HOW IT IS CHECKED. The command list is DERIVED, by parsing the protocol
enums for variants carrying a reply channel; this file supplies only the
classification, which cannot be derived. A command that appears in the
source and not here fails the gate, and so does one that appears here and
not in the source. See scripts/test-synchronous-surface-contract.sh.
producer_answers_locally:
yes    - the producer answers without crossing, always
partly - answered locally for some inputs; the rest cross
no     - every call crosses
n_a    - not reachable from content; host lifecycle
reply:
always   - the variant always carries a reply channel
optional - the channel is an Option; see callers_supplying_a_reply
REMOVED: GLCmd::IsEnabled. It used to be here classified `no` -- every call
crossed -- with a note saying it was shadowable in principle and not
shadowed. It is shadowed now: 02_webgl_context.js keeps the ten toggleable
capabilities in one integer per context, seeded at the GL initial state and
reset on context loss, so isEnabled answers without leaving the thread and
the command has no callers left. It was also the one query where crossing
gave a worse answer: the GL context is shared with Skia, which toggles
GL_STENCIL_TEST inside its own batches, and the engine toggles
GL_SCISSOR_TEST around blits -- so the driver's bit is not content's bit,
while WebGL defines isEnabled purely in terms of content's own calls.

GLCmd::GetParameter.note: The seven *_BINDING queries come from the facade's own shadow, and the ten capability enums come from the same producer-side capability shadow that answers isEnabled -- the spec defines getParameter(BLEND) and isEnabled(BLEND) as one answer, so they must not be able to disagree. Every other pname crosses. The device limits and the four strings are constants of the implementation and could be cached after the first query; the *_BITS values, SAMPLES and SAMPLE_BUFFERS could NOT, because in GL ES they describe the currently bound framebuffer.

GLCmd::GetAttribLocation.note: Cached per program and name, so one crossing per distinct name, at load.

GLCmd::GetUniformLocation.note: Cached per program and name, invalidated on deleteProgram.

GLCmd::GetShaderParameter.note: SHADER_TYPE is immutable and cached; COMPILE_STATUS crosses.

GLCmd::GetProgramInfoLog.note: Diagnostic, at load, and only on failure paths in practice.

GLCmd::GetActiveAttrib.note: Introspection at load; Emscripten exports walk every attribute of every program. Cached per (program, index) in the facade now, so the walk crosses once per entry instead of once per call, and `_invalidateProgramCaches` drops it on relink -- relinking renumbers the active attributes, so a cache that survived it would hand back plausible records belonging to the previous link.

GLCmd::GetActiveUniform.note: Introspection at load; the same walk as GetActiveAttrib and usually larger. Cached and invalidated the same way.

GLCmd::GetUniformBlockIndex.note: Introspection at load. Cached per (program, name) and invalidated on relink -- the note here used to read 'cacheable the way getUniformLocation is, and not cached'.

GLCmd::GetTransformFeedbackVarying.note: Introspection at load, rare. Cached per (program, index) and dropped on relink, on the same path as GetActiveAttrib and GetActiveUniform -- the class is closed rather than three-quarters done, because the next reader of these three would have to work out why the fourth was different.

GLCmd::CheckFramebufferStatus.note: Called after framebuffer setup, and by some engines every time a render target changes.

GLCmd::ClientWaitSync.note: A fence probe. Designed to be polled every frame, and the deadline it gets is the ten-second one.

GLCmd::GetQueryParameter.note: Timer and occlusion queries, polled every frame, on the same ten-second deadline.

GLCmd::ReadPixels.note: The pixels are on the renderer's side by definition. No producer-side answer exists.

GLCmd::ShaderSource.note: The runtime always passes resp: None. The channel is unused capability, not a crossing.

GLCmd::AttachShader.note: As ShaderSource: the runtime always passes resp: None.

Canvas2DCmd::MeasureText.note: A JS-side cache keyed on font and string, in front of an inline shared measurer when the host installs one. Across a process boundary the measurer is not inline and the cache miss crosses.

Canvas2DCmd::GetImageData.note: The pixels are on the renderer's side. The snapshot path defers the copy but not the answer.

Canvas2DCmd::ReadSnapshotPixels.note: The second half of the snapshot path: the read that happens when content actually touches the pixels.

RenderCommand::LoadFont.note: Once per font, at load. The answer is whether the face parsed.

RenderCommand::GetTextLineHeight.note: Per-frame in label-heavy UI, which is why it shares measureText's four-millisecond deadline class. Cached in 04_font.js by (family, size, bold, italic) -- a pure function of those -- and invalidated by the __migoFontEpoch counter loadFont already bumps for measureText's cache, so there is one invalidation rule rather than two. The cache is bounded because its key space is content's.

CanvasCmd::GetInfo.note: Host lifecycle: the canvas size, asked once when a canvas is constructed.

CanvasCmd::DestroyCanvas.note: Host lifecycle; the reply is what makes teardown ordered.

CanvasCmd::LoadImage.note: Host-side decode; content reaches it through an asynchronous Image.
